players.product: York chillers for hyperscale data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q3 organic sales rose 10%, led by strength in applied HVAC, with systems sales up 11% and service up 7%; APPLIED HVAC DELIVERED HIGH-TEENS GROWTH SUPPORTED BY DATA CENTER DEMAND. Adjusted segment EBITDA margin expanded 220 basis points to 20% and adjusted EBIT margin expanded 260 basis points to 17%. Adjusted EPS was $1.42, up 35% year over year and ahead of guidance. By region, Americas organic revenue rose 11% with segment EBITDA margin up 260 basis points to 21%; EMEA rose 1% (margin up 20 basis points to 14%) held back by the Middle East conflict, which is about 10% of EMEA; APAC grew 15% led by 20% systems growth with margin up 180 basis points to 21%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 organic sales +10% (systems +11%, service +7%, applied HVAC high teens); adjusted EBIT margin 17% (+260bps); adjusted EPS $1.42 (+35%)

quarterly_data.signal: Orders rose 27% with momentum sustained above 25% through fiscal 2026: systems orders grew 40% while service orders grew 4%. The AMERICAS LED WITH ORDERS UP 37%, driven by sustained demand from data centers and other mission-critical environments; EMEA orders rose 6% and APAC 12%. BACKLOG INCREASED 32% YEAR OVER YEAR TO A RECORD $21 BILLION, which management says underpins both the near-term outlook and the long-term growth algorithm. The non-data-center pipeline is also growing almost double digits.
quarterly_data.figure: Orders +27% (systems +40%); Americas orders +37%; backlog +32% YoY to a record $21B

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance was raised. For fiscal Q4: organic revenue growth of 9-10%, operating leverage of 45-50% and adjusted EPS of approximately $1.55. For full-year fiscal 2026: organic revenue growth of approximately 8%, up from approximately 6% previously; operating leverage of 45-50%; and adjusted EPS raised to approximately $5.05, roughly 35% growth and $0.50 above the original guide at the start of the year, with adjusted free cash flow conversion of approximately 100%. The long-term algorithm introduced at Going to Gemba Day is high single-digit revenue growth, operating leverage of more than 30%, double-digit adjusted EPS growth and adjusted free cash flow conversion of approximately 95-100%; management expects operating leverage to run ABOVE 30% for the next 12 to 18, maybe 24 months.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 organic revenue growth raised to ~8% (from ~6%); adjusted EPS raised to ~$5.05 (+~35%); Q4 EPS ~$1.55

quarterly_data.signal: Data center revenue will land in the HIGH TEENS AS A PERCENTAGE OF REVENUE for fiscal 2026 and is growing much faster than the rest of the portfolio - very healthy double digits, higher in some subsegments. Over the next THREE TO FIVE YEARS management expects data centers to become ONE THIRD OF THE COMPANY by revenue, and describes the mix as extremely accretive to the enterprise. As the installed base expands on double-digit systems growth, service attachment rates should improve and generate strong service growth, fuelling the data center mix profitably. CEO Joakim Weidemanis framed the era directly: 'this is the age of thermal management.'
quarterly_data.figure: Data center ~high teens % of FY2026 revenue, expected to reach one third of company revenue in three to five years

quarterly_data.signal: Johnson Controls introduced an AI FACTORY ABSORPTION CHILLER REFERENCE DESIGN GUIDE, which it says demonstrates how advanced thermal management can REDUCE COOLING ELECTRICAL DEMAND BY APPROXIMATELY 44% by converting waste heat into productive cooling. Because those savings free power for compute without increasing on-site generation, management claims the potential for BILLIONS OF DOLLARS OF ADDITIONAL REVENUE OVER THE LIFE OF A 1 GIGAWATT FACILITY for the customer. The approach builds on more than 65 years of YORK absorption innovation. Management noted thermal management can represent ABOUT A THIRD OF POWER in a data center, so multiple percentage points of thermal efficiency are very meaningful - and that what JCI is working on 'goes well beyond a couple of percentage points.' Efficiency now matters more because power availability constrains where data centers can be sited.
quarterly_data.figure: Absorption chiller reference design cuts cooling electrical demand by ~44%; thermal management is ~1/3 of data center power

quarterly_data.signal: The CDU (coolant distribution unit) business reaches revenue: Johnson Controls WILL START SHIPPING CDUs THIS QUARTER, with most testing and validation complete and some hyperscaler validation still in progress, and it has RECENTLY RECEIVED NVIDIA CERTIFICATION. The CDU pipeline is 'well beyond the hundreds of millions and has now reached $1 BILLION,' built on JCI's Alloy investment plus pilots and early orders. Management frames CDUs as expanding total addressable market per megawatt within a broader thermal management solution set.
quarterly_data.figure: CDU shipments start this quarter; CDU pipeline reached $1B; NVIDIA certification received

quarterly_data.signal: On the chiller-versus-liquid-cooling debate, management pushed back directly: as rack densities increase and new chips are used, the heat generated in data centers keeps rising and thermal management becomes more critical, so speculation about reduced demand for chillers is 'a very nominal impact if any.' Air handling demand continues with the Silent-Aire franchise increasing, CDUs become more important as liquid cooling is implemented, and controls matter as well. The strategy is explicitly to keep increasing DOLLARS PER MEGAWATT across the whole thermal management chain - including the Armada modular container, which is 'loaded with everything we make.'

Capacity and supply chain: Johnson Controls says it is more vertically integrated than others in its industry, controlling the manufacturing and cost of goods of all FIVE SUBSYSTEMS that make up an HVAC chiller, which gives it more control of its own supply chain; bottlenecks occur occasionally in a high-growth environment. Meaningful physical plant investments made about two years ago are ramping slightly AHEAD of expectations. At the Airside Center of Excellence, applying the business system MORE THAN QUADRUPLED CAPACITY on the computer room air handler line WITHOUT SIGNIFICANT CAPITAL INVESTMENT, while achieving 100% on-time delivery, halving customer lead times, shrinking manufacturing floor space by more than 30% and cutting inventory by 50%. Management expects to need some new physical capacity at this growth rate but believes the business system buys time to ramp it. JCI operates approximately 40 manufacturing facilities worldwide.
quarterly_data.figure: Computer room air handler line capacity more than quadrupled without significant capital investment; lead times halved; inventory cut 50%

quarterly_data.signal: How hyperscalers actually award thermal work, per CEO Joakim Weidemanis: large data center customers architect their facilities and make equipment choices during design, often sending groups of engineers to sit with JCI engineers for A WEEK OR TEN DAYS - being 'designed in.' They typically pick ONE OR TWO partners per architecture that they plan to build multiple times over the following two to three years, and THE AWARD IS TYPICALLY SPLIT, with someone rarely getting all of it. A supplier that executes better on lead times with fewer supply chain issues can secure more than initially expected. Service is usually part of the initial selection, where JCI leans on a field organisation roughly TWICE THE SCALE of its nearest competitor. Asked directly whether JCI is gaining share, Weidemanis said: 'We think we are gaining share in the categories that we focus on. Absolutely.'

Edge and modular: Johnson Controls collaborates with and holds an investment in ARMADA, building modular solutions described as 'data centers in a shipping container' in JCI factories and including everything Johnson Controls makes. They are a couple of megawatts today and are forward deployed in remote locations, oil and gas, and defense. Management believes not all future data centers will be mega sites like 1 gigawatt facilities and expects decentralized, close-to-the-edge deployments to keep growing; the TAM is described as significant but still in formation, with more detail promised over the next couple of quarters. Balance sheet: approximately $600 million of cash on hand, net debt down to 1.9x - below the long-term target range - and year-to-date adjusted free cash flow of $2.1 billion. Fire and Security revenue was flat against a flat underlying global market, with management targeting mid-to-high single-digit growth there over time.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$600M cash; net debt 1.9x (below target range); year-to-date adjusted FCF $2.1B
